codes.name: Civil disagreement
codes.definition: Practices and norms for holding differences of opinion without hostility or rupture.

highlights.insight_text: A Ben Franklin story illustrates trading winning arguments for asking questions to keep relationships.

evidence.text: I read a story years ago and it was either in a biography or autobiography of Ben Franklin. And he said when as a younger man he was very argumentative and he was very smart, very, very eloquent and he would defeat a lot of people in debates. Felt really good about himself, but had no friendships, had no relationships. And he began reevaluate how he communicated and discovered that if he would ask questions, rather than hit him with a hammer, if he would ask questions, he could still guide the conversation some. But he was able to build those relationships and have mutual respect and cooperation. A lot of times questions are a great place to start.
